profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at National Grid
profile.summary: After the realization set in that I will not be following in the footsteps of Guy Fieri and trying food for a living, I have decided to stay in school and pursue my passions in business and computer science. I am a well driven student, diligent engineer, and innovator with a proven record of solving complex problems from debugging software to creating a budget for a company. I am committed on tackling challenging tasks and meeting goals independently as well as within a team environment. I am always eager to further develop my professional skillset from not only in the classroom, but from professionals I enjoy working alongside with.

company.name: University of Massachusetts Amherst Finance Society

positions.title: Student Member
positions.description: The UMass Finance Society welcomes all majors! As a member we meet weekly to discuss and participate in active conversations on current financial news and future career paths. The society also helps promote networking skills in meetings to further career development.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: As a teaching assistant for the Department of Resource Economics, I lead students through tasks of Excel, Microsoft Access, and SAS. I was able to build personal connections with students (ranging from sophomores to freshmen) allowing them to be comfortable for inquiring aid on course material.

positions.title: Finance Intern
positions.description: Coravin, Inc. was one of the world's Top 10 Most Innovative Companies of 2016 in Food! I was fortunate enough to work among such passionate employees . During my seasonal employment at Coravin, I spent my time working within the financial department. I handled the accounts payable/reimbursement process to vendors and employees as well as examined and recorded financial transactions, daily receipts and balances through Excel.

positions.title: Lab Technician
positions.description: Working at LensCrafters was always welcoming! I was blessed with the opportunity to learn from incredible managers and other Lab Technicians on not just the production of high quality eyewear, but the further development of my professional prowess that I carry out even today. During my time at LensCrafters I utilized product knowledge to determine the best manufacturing process for routine and special orders in a way to produce top quality glasses. I even performed multiple tasks simultaneously with accuracy and thoroughness despite time pressures and customer volume. I was constantly attentive to detail with all measurements, calculations, equipment settings and defective product.
